summary: Iteration 51 — Stripe Subscription Integration Testing (Backend Only). 27/27 tests PASS (100%). All subscription flows verified: plan listing, Stripe Checkout Session creation (mode=subscription), double-subscription guard (409), cancellation (at_period_end + immediate admin), webhook processing (created/updated/deleted/invoice.paid/invoice.payment_failed), pricing engine exemptions, plan deactivation with benefit preservation. One critical production bug fixed in payment_routes.py (webhook early-return blocker).

critical.issue: CRITICAL BUG FIXED: Subscription webhook events (customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted, invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed) were silently ignored. Root cause: the early return `if not payment_id: return` in payment_routes.py (line ~342) was placed BEFORE the dispatch to handle_subscription_event(). Since subscription events never have payment_id in metadata, they always triggered the early return and handle_subscription_event() was NEVER called. Fix: moved subscription event dispatch before the early return check.

minor.issue: CODE QUALITY: The entire module content (all dataclasses + singleton instantiation) is duplicated starting at line 341 (lines 341-415 duplicate lines 28-339). Python overwrites class definitions at module level so runtime behavior is correct (second definition wins), but this is a significant maintenance hazard. Should be deduplicated.
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty ('') → no signature verification. All valid JSON accepted without Stripe-Signature header. Expected in test env, must be set in production.

rca_of_issue.bug: Webhook dispatcher in payment_routes.py had subscription event dispatch AFTER early-return guard
rca_of_issue.root_cause: Lines ~342-344 checked `if not payment_id: return` before reaching the subscription event dispatch block (~lines 413-418). Since subscription events (customer.subscription.*, invoice.*) never include payment_id in metadata (they have plan_id/user_id/product_type), they always triggered the early return. handle_subscription_event() was never called for any subscription webhook, making the entire webhook-based subscription lifecycle non-functional.
rca_of_issue.reproduction: POST /api/webhook/stripe with body {type: 'customer.subscription.created', data: {object: {..., metadata: {plan_id: 'plan_basic', user_id: 'xxx', product_type: 'subscription'}}}} → returns {received: true} but nothing written to user_subscriptions table
rca_of_issue.fix_applied: Moved the subscription event dispatch block (import + await handle_subscription_event()) to BEFORE the early-return check. Removed the now-redundant duplicate dispatch block that was at the end of the function.
